source.body:
## Goal

Extend ChemE-as-Code with an optional social life cycle assessment (S-LCA) workflow so process alternatives can be assessed for social supply-chain risks alongside technical performance, economics and environmental LCA.

**Priority: low / future platform extension.** Schedule after the foundations for reliable environmental LCA and economic assessment. Start with transparent hotspot screening and deepen the assessment as evidence becomes available.

## Proposed scope

- [ ] Define a versioned social inventory linked to the process inventory: production locations, feedstock and equipment origins, supplier sectors, expenditure and labour estimates where applicable.
- [ ] Record system boundaries, functional unit, data year, sources, assumptions, missing data and uncertainty; distinguish site-specific evidence from country/sector proxies.
- [ ] Evaluate integration with an existing assessment engine and databases, including openLCA, PSILCA and the Social Hotspots Database. Document access, licensing and redistribution constraints before selecting an approach.
- [ ] Provide reproducible mapping from engineering inputs to database activities, including units, currency/base-year conversion and activity-variable assumptions where required.
- [ ] Generate category-level hotspot results, contribution analysis and a list of evidence gaps.
- [ ] Support explicitly defined sourcing, location and technology scenarios with a common functional unit and comparable boundaries.
- [ ] Expose reusable calculation tools through the platform's CLI/MCP and an accompanying agent workflow; reuse the existing assessment architecture where practical.
- [ ] Develop one worked example with S-LCA expert review.

## Methodological requirements

Use the UNEP S-LCA guidelines as a starting point and document the selected indicators and assessment method.

Country/sector hotspot results indicate potential risk; they do not establish actual performance or misconduct at an individual supplier or plant. A flowsheet alone is insufficient to infer working conditions or community impacts.

Agents may propose mappings, gather cited evidence, identify missing inputs and explain results. Calculations must use explicit methods and data; agents must not invent social scores. Keep indicators separate initially rather than introducing an opaque aggregate sustainability score.

Licensed source datasets must remain outside public repositories unless redistribution is permitted. Make example inputs and published outputs reproducible to the extent allowed by their terms.

## Candidate demonstration

Green ammonia with alternative electricity and electrolyser supply chains, holding ammonia output constant. Investigate whether lower climate impacts coincide with lower social supply-chain risks, with no assumed winner. Select the final example based on data availability and expert input.

## Acceptance criteria for an initial screening release

- [ ] One documented example can be regenerated from versioned inputs and mappings.
- [ ] Results identify their method, database version, boundaries, assumptions and data gaps.
- [ ] Missing data remain explicit and are not treated as zero risk.
- [ ] Scenario differences can be traced to inventory, sourcing or mapping changes.
- [ ] Reports clearly distinguish hotspot screening from a detailed site-specific assessment.

## References

- [UNEP S-LCA Guidelines (2020)](https://www.lifecycleinitiative.org/library/guidelines-for-social-life-cycle-assessment-of-products-and-organisations-2020/)
- [openLCA social assessment documentation](https://greendelta.github.io/openLCA2-manual/advanced_top/social_aspects.html)
- [PSILCA](https://psilca.net/)
